newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays under pressure on offshore selling.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays under pressure on offshore selling.

text.p: The ringgit remained pressured by offshore selling but dollar gains were again capped by Bank Negara Malaysia, dealers said.
They said an agent of the central bank aggressively sold the dollar/ringgit each time it touched the 2.5250 level.

"Some U.S. and Japanese names were buying up dollar/ringgit but once again it was capped below 2.5250, thanks to Bank Negara's presence throughout the session," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
Dollar/ringgit tested 2.5250 several times in the past week, unsuccessfully, due to the central bank support.

Bank Negara on Wednesday intervened directly, selling the dollar at 2.5250, to protect the ringgit after Thailand announced a managed float of the baht. It also sold the dollar at that level through an agent bank during London trading, dealers said.

It was the first time in many years that Bank Negara used its own name while intervening in the foreign exchange market. It usually uses a broker or some of Malaysia's biggest banks for its market operations.
Fear of spillover effect from Thailand was cited as one reason for continued Bank Negara operations.
Dealers said they expected the dollar's upside to be limited as stop-loss orders were building up around 2.5265/75.

There has also been talk in the market that local corporates were asked to hold off any dollar purchases until the Thai situation subsided or to lower their orders to around 2.5200 instead of 2.5230/40 to avoid excessive moves in the ringgit.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5240/50 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5245/50 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
